changes.title: Detailed maps of European wetlands reveal overlooked patches of ecosystems
changes.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02211-2 Satellite images have been analysed by a machine-learning algorithm to produce high-resolution maps of wetland environments — a boon for conservation efforts.

changes.title: Daily briefing: CRISPR gets an AI-designed upgrade
changes.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 July 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02272-3 Synthetic CRISPR proteins edit the genome more efficiently than their natural counterparts. Plus, a rocky exoplanet with an atmosphere and the mathematical wonderland of footballs.

changes.title: Funding milestone detected
changes.summary: Researchers have copied massive quantities of publicly available climate and environmental data from NASA onto a Swiss supercomputer to train artificial intelligence models—and for safekeeping amid U.S. funding cuts.

changes.title: AI ‘ghosts’ can comfort mourners — even when the bots get the facts wrong
changes.summary: A small study suggests emotional fit, not perfect accuracy, may make chatbot versions of dead loved ones feel real.

changes.title: Dr. Jill Lepore on why AI backlash is vital for the future
changes.summary: Today, I’m talking with Harvard professor and New Yorker staff writer Dr. Jill Lepore about her new book, The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State , which comes out on August 25. Jill is one of the best writers there is at identifying institutional patterns in history, and Decoder is a show about systems, so this book.

changes.title: Developer ecosystem expanded
changes.summary: Nature, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02214-z As automated tools accelerate both the discovery and the exploitation of software vulnerabilities, organizations must redesign their defences and workflows to keep pace.

changes.title: A global capital for AI safety is emerging — and it’s not in Silicon Valley
changes.summary: Nature, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01389-9 The United Kingdom is gaining influence through its growing AI-safety ecosystem.

changes.title: AI tool reveals climate shifts may have fueled bursts of bird evolution
changes.summary: University of Michigan researchers have used an AI tool to demonstrate that birds in the group Passeriformes evolved in rapid evolutionary bursts and that these bursts frequently coincided with climate shifts throughout Earth's history.
